original_value: As multisourcing becomes a widely adopted strategy in dynamic procurement planning, firms inevitably source from suppliers with dependent material flows, and such supply dependence, created by common second-tier suppliers or a common economic environment, is often positive. We show that firms can experience significant profit loss when implementing a policy computed based on a model that ignores the dependence among suppliers’ stochastic material flows. The profit loss is particularly significant when a firm earns a low margin or faces an unreliable and fragmented supplier base. Analysis of the firm’s dynamic multisourcing strategy under dependent supply uncertainties, however, is challenging. By expanding the space of ordering decision to a class of contingency policies, we identify conditions under which the dynamic planning model has a concave transformation. This approach allows us to characterize the optimal procurement policy. Moreover, our analysis suggests that the firm may order more from a less reliable supplier than from a more reliable one who charges the same procurement cost. The order allocation to the less reliable supplier can be even larger when the capacities are more dependent. Though the analysis of our base model is conducted for dependent supply capacities that are independent across periods, we show that the results can be generalized to Markov-modulated supplies or general supply functions that are stochastically linear in midpoint.  This paper was accepted by Noah Gans, stochastic models and simulation.

result.paraphrase: As multisourcing has become a common approach in dynamic procurement planning, firms inevitably buy from suppliers with interdependent material flows, and such dependence—arising from shared second-tier suppliers or a common economic environment—is often positive. We demonstrate that substantial profit losses can occur when a policy is implemented from a model that ignores dependence among suppliers’ stochastic material flows. These losses are especially large when margins are low or the supplier base is unreliable and fragmented. Analyzing a firm’s dynamic multisourcing strategy under dependent supply uncertainty is difficult, however. By enlarging the ordering decision space to a class of contingency policies, we identify conditions under which the dynamic planning model admits a concave transformation. This enables us to characterize the optimal procurement policy. Our analysis also indicates that a firm may order more from a less reliable supplier than from a more reliable one when both charge the same procurement cost. The allocation to the less reliable supplier can be even higher when capacities are more dependent. Although the base model is analyzed for dependent supply capacities that are independent across periods, we show that the results extend to Markov-modulated supplies and to general supply functions that are stochastically linear in midpoint. This paper was accepted by Noah Gans, stochastic models and simulation.
